label: early token right after a 0 (esp. i; 0 0 i strongest)
explanation: Fires only in the original phase at positions 1-3, almost always on the input right after a digit 0 (prev_tok=0 holds 96% of mass). At t=1 it fires only on 0 i (on every such step). At t=2 it fires on 0 followed by any token when the first token is 0, g, y, q, e, t or 2, and on 0 i for any first token. Strongest on i: 0 0 i reaches the max activation. 0 0 x for other x and g/y/q 0 x are weaker (around 0.3x max). Small t=3 tail (x 0 0 i). Never fires at t=0, at t>=4, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Mostly does not fire after 0 when the first token is outside that set, unless the current token is i.

issues: The claims about where it fires hold up. 100% of activation mass is in the original phase. There are 0 activations at t=0, at t>=4, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Activations sit at t=1 (25% of mass), t=2 (73%) and t=3 (1.5%). prev_tok=0 carries 96.3% of the mass.

The t=1 claim holds. (t==1)&(prev_tok==0)&(in_tok==i) scores precision 1.0, and nothing fires at t=1 outside it. (t==1)&(prev_tok==0) on its own has only 3.5% precision, so at t=1 it does not fire after a 0 in general.

The label overclaims a little. 'Early token right after a 0' leaves out the first-token gating at t=2 and the restriction to i at t=1. For 0 x at t=2, firing depends strongly on first_tok. With first_tok in {0,g,y,q} precision is 0.985. With first_tok in {e,t,2} precision is only 0.37-0.54, and it varies by in_tok (for first_tok=e, a subset of in_toks fires with precision 1.0).

Most of the remaining misses are a weak t=2 tail where prev_tok is not 0 and in_tok is i (e.g. 'g g i', '0 y i', 'q g i'). This is about 11% of active steps but only 3.5% of mass, at around 0.1-0.3 of the max. Adding it gives low precision (0.11), so treat it as a weak tail rather than a fixable class.

Dropping '2' from the first_tok set gives a small gain: test precision 0.864, recall 0.834, F1 0.848 (vs 0.833 for the recorded predicate), mass recall 0.952. This is a minor refinement, not a refutation.

The magnitude ordering is plausible from mass per step. 0 0 i: 19 steps, 1.65% of mass, about 8.7e-4 per step. t=1 0 i: about 4.4e-4 per step. t=2 0 x with first_tok in the set: about 2.3e-4 per step. That is consistent with '0 0 i' being strongest and the others being about 0.3-0.5x.
skeptic.revised_label: t=1 '0 i', or t=2 input right after a 0 when the first token is 0/g/y/q (also i after a 0); 0 0 i strongest

final_label: t=1 '0 i', or t=2 input right after a 0 when the first token is 0/g/y/q (also i after a 0); 0 0 i strongest
